purpose: Machine-readable form of the Stage 13-16 readiness facts used by the offline coverage planner (product_tool/coverage). Every claim names repo evidence; nothing here was re-verified with a network request. Facts override adapter_profiles.v1.json only where a later stage proved that profile stale. Stage 18: a Product page fixture proves only the host, market, catalog category and page template that were actually observed (family_facts.<family>.scopes); it is never carried to the rest of the brand.

statuses.meaning: A working adapter wired into worker.run_once() covers the brand and can reach the product page: an exact URL is on record, or the adapter's own confirmed discovery route resolves it from the catalog code.
A working adapter exists but has no confirmed exact product URL for this row and no confirmed discovery route; run_once() would stop at official_url_needed.

The official host is verified and the saved Product page evidence covers identity, specifications and media (a full-value card, or a structural sample with all three layers), but no adapter is wired into run_once().
The official host is verified but there is no Product page evidence sufficient to build an adapter (none, or a structural sample missing identity/specifications/media).
The only official host(s) returned 401/403/429/challenge or were paused by a recorded block; no further requests are allowed until a human clears the host.
The catalog row or saved evidence shows the exact model/variant cannot be settled (same seller article under several catalog units, or a confirmed regional/variant mismatch).
No verified official route, unresolved brand, missing brand or article, or a data anomaly a person must decide.

wave_readiness_criteria.text: Exact identity is decided by the source's own model and variant signals (the model name or code fields the page publishes, plus a variant discriminator such as colour, size, capacity or layout taken from a structured field), not by finding the seller SKU on the official site: seller SKUs such as CFI-ZCT1W_cosmic_red are catalog labels and may never appear on a page. exact_variant needs both model and variant to match; without a variant discriminator the result is exact_model at most. A manufacturer or regional code that the page does publish must not disagree with the catalog code: a confirmed mismatch (7G7A4AA#ABA on the page, #ACB in the catalog) blocks exact_variant and yields base_code_confirmed or identity_conflict, never a silent pass.

Per category in scope: at least one positive and one negative variant fixture (wrong colour/region/size/layout), taken from the same host and market as the scope; the negative never becomes exact_variant. A fixture from another category, market or page template does not count.
Specifications extracted as name/value pairs, each with source URL and evidence; unit and value are not rewritten.
The full gallery that belongs to this exact variant is captured; images of other variants, banners and icons are excluded with a recorded reason.
A document is attached only from a direct link whose content or page names the exact model; regulatory papers are not instructions; absence is stated as a gap, not filled from a neighbour model.
worker.run_once() replays a catalog row offline against saved fixtures and finishes done or needs_review with the expected reason for every fixture.
The coverage executor saves a checkpoint per row, and a second pass over the same checkpoint makes no new calls and repeats no completed row.
Every fetch goes through PolicyAwareFetcher (allowlist, redirect checks, budget, persisted log); a recorded 401/403/429/challenge stops the host across a restart.
`python -m product_tool.coverage delta` against the pre-adapter plan shows the promised movement out of the wave's source statuses and no unit moving into ready_to_run without a positive fixture.

confirmed_exact_urls.rule: Only rows whose saved evidence reached identity exact_variant on an official page for the catalog market are counted as exact URLs on record. An adapter built for the family can use them as positive fixtures the day it lands.

not_counted.reason: Stage 9 reached exact_model only: the page is the US web-store (direct.playstation.com/en-us, market differs from the catalog) and two catalog rows (CFI-ZCT1J 02 and CFI-ZCT1W_cosmic_red) share the colour, so the row cannot be told apart. The absence of the CFI code from the page is not the reason; 25 catalog DualSense units differ by colour/revision code.
Stage 10.2's page is the Xbox Series S line page, not an exact-variant page; the catalog-vs-page match is line-wide.

scope_rules.rule: A fixture is a scope: (host, market, catalog categories, page template). A unit is covered only if its own catalog category is listed in a scope whose layers are complete and whose market matches the catalog's. A family with no scope covering the unit's category is needs_product_page_fixture, never official_route_no_adapter.
scope_rules.sufficient_when: identity, specifications and media are all 'observed' (a scope may also declare fixture_level 'full_value' when a value-level card was built)
scope_rules.market_rule: market_matches_catalog is stated per scope with its reason. A page observed in a foreign store (a US web-store, a German country site) does not prove the catalog's market; the unit waits for a fixture in the catalog market or an explicit decision.
scope_rules.categories_are: exact catalog category strings (Категория column); nothing is matched by keyword or by brand

shared_seller_sku.rule: The same seller article under several brands or categories is recorded as a risk flag (seller_sku_shared_across_brand / _category) and the unit is classified by its own route. It becomes identity_conflict only when the catalog titles of the units carry model tokens and share none of them (real contradiction). Titles without a model token are 'uninformative': the risk stays, no conflict is declared.
shared_seller_sku.model_token: alphanumeric token with a digit and a letter, at least 3 characters, not a bare quantity (20W, 350mm, 12V, 30шт)
